- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.40) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10% relative to prior high.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 7–14 days — cap forecast at 1–2% below true peak or use 3-day moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (e.g., 0.0–0.30), model tends to overestimate mean — adjust downward by 2–5% for 3–7 day horizon.
- When sentiment turns positive after a downtrend, model often fails to capture momentum — increase forecast slope slightly (e.g., +0.5–1.0% per day) for 5–10 day horizon.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 70–75), reduce forecast by 3–5% for next 7 days unless sentiment confirms breakout.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., -0.30 → +0.20 → -0.30), model tends to lag — add 1–2 days of lagged sentiment to forecast adjustment (e.g., use 2-day sentiment average for 5-day forecast).
